title: Canonical scalar map of integral geometric fibres
statement: Let l be prime, Y a Noetherian separated scheme on which l is invertible, y a geometric point, E and L finite extensions of Q_l and i:E→L a Q_l-algebra embedding. Use the coefficient rings and scalar-extension systems of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. The integral geometric fibre M of a lisse integral E-sheaf is finite over O_E and its projection to level n is surjective with kernel (pi_E)^(n+1)M. There is a unique O_L-linear comparison O_L tensor_O_E M → (i_*F)_y whose level-n image of 1 tensor z, after the specified level isomorphism, is the germ of 1 tensor s whenever the source projection of z is the germ of s. This comparison is natural in the integral sheaf.

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b)-d), pp. 146-147; finite-level scalar stalk comparison; adic reconstruction as in Stacks Tag 09B8

proof.text: Apply the stated adic reconstruction theorem to the stalk tower. Finite lisse sheaf stalks are finite modules; the annihilation property follows by representing a stalk element by a section. Identify the categorical limit with the sections submodule to transfer finite generation and the surjective quotient projection formulas.

At target level n apply the adjunction unit to the source stalk at the ramification ceiling index. Compose scalar/stalk comparison, restriction of coefficients, and the inverse of the recorded finite-level isomorphism. The pure-germ formula identifies the result with the germ of 1 tensor s.

The scalar system transition and map equations give compatibility and naturality: on pure section generators both composites agree, hence they agree by adjunction and stalk coprojection extensionality. The compatible maps form a cone, whose limit map is the adjoint of the comparison.

Uniqueness follows by adjunction, limit extensionality and representation of every stalk element by a germ. Define the public map from this proved unique existence; its specification and naturality follow from uniqueness.
